subject: Clarify: retention windows, backups, and explicit non-training guarantee
messages:
From: Anne Collins <anne.collins@finnobank.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify: retention windows, backups, and explicit non-training guarantee

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — helpful. Our security team has a couple of follow-ups before we move to a pilot: specifically around your statement that Redwood 'does not train on our data.' Could you confirm what that means across the following dimensions?

- Hosted (Redwood API) vs Dedicated vs Private deployments — does any customer content ever get ingested into training/fine-tuning pipelines?
- Short-term caches (KV cache, prefix caches) and streaming buffers — are these persisted, and if so for how long?
- Backups and snapshots — if we ask for deletion, do backups get purged? What are the timelines?
- Auditability — can you provide evidence that data was removed (audit logs, signed attestation)?

We need concrete timelines and exceptions in plain language for our legal/security reviewers. Attaching the intake spreadsheet we use for vendors (not attaching here).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we’re aiming to decide by end of next week.

Best,
Anne
Anne Collins
Director, Cloud Security
FinnoBank
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify: retention windows, backups, and explicit non-training guarantee

Hi Anne — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: Redwood does not use customer content to train our public or internal model training pipelines. I've looped in Rishi (Security) and Neha (Privacy/Legal) to provide the detailed breakdown and attach SOC2 artifacts.

Rishi/Neha — could you reply with retention windows for hosted vs dedicated vs private, details about backups/snapshots, and what evidence we can provide for deletion requests? Anne is the security lead on the FinnoBank evaluation.

Chloe Martin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Anne Collins <anne.collins@finnobank.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: retention windows, backups, and explicit non-training guarantee

Hi Anne — hi Chloe,

Thanks for the question. Below is a concise, engineer-friendly summary followed by a few important caveats. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30‑minute compliance call and we’ll bring our infra/ops lead.

Executive summary (plain words):
- Redwood does not include customer-provided content in model training datasets. We have technical and contractual controls that prevent customer content from being routed into any training/fine-tuning pipelines.

Technical details and retention specifics:
1) Hosted API (SaaS):
   - Request payloads: stored encrypted at rest for debugging/traceability for a default of 30 days. This window is configurable per-customer via a DPA addendum (we can reduce to 7/0 days for enterprise plans).
   - Aggregated telemetry (usage metrics, token counts): retained 365 days for billing/analytics; does NOT contain full customer content.
   - Short-term runtime caches (KV/attention caches): ephemeral in memory and persisted only for active session acceleration; persisted snapshots are not used for training and are rotated within 24–72 hours.
   - Backups/snapshots: metadata/backups are kept on a rolling 7-day snapshot schedule by default. Backups do not feed training; they are encrypted and access-controlled.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
   - Customer data remains logically isolated and stored on your dedicated pool. Retention policies are per-contract. Default debug traces are kept 30 days unless contractually changed. There is no pipeline that copies dedicated-customer content into Redwood training workflows.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
   - For private deployments you control the infrastructure and encryption keys. By default Redwood’s control plane does not ingest customer content for training. If a customer enables telemetry sharing, that is explicit and opt-in.

Deletion and backups:
- Deletion request handling: when you request deletion for hosted data, we initiate purging of active stores within 72 hours and purge snapshot chains within a maximum of 30 days, depending on snapshot retention policies and cloud provider retention semantics. For dedicated/private, we follow the agreed retention in the contract and can add accelerated snapshot purges as part of onboarding.
- Note: immutable backups retained by a third-party cloud provider (e.g., if you require immutable WORM backups) can extend the effective deletion window; we’ll document exceptions in the DPA.

Training safeguards and verification:
- Training fences: customer identifiers and content are tagged by default so training pipelines exclude those namespaces. We also maintain a training audit log that lists datasets used for any model update (available to customers under NDA for enterprise arrangements).
- Evidence: we can provide a signed attestation and relevant train-exclusion audit logs for a given time range. SOC2 artifacts (attached) describe our controls.

Caveats and rare cases:
- Debug snapshots created during incident investigations may be retained longer for triage; these are rare and require approval with an auditable change ticket.
- If a customer explicitly opts into model improvement programs (opt-in for fine-tuning), that will be contractual and visible in the console with explicit consent.

Attachments: SOC2-logs-sampling.pdf (sample control descriptions), deletion-process-diagram.png (high-level flow).

If you want specific retention numbers we can propose the SLA language (e.g., 7-day debug retention, 30-day snapshot purge) and add it to the DPA.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
From: Anne Collins <anne.collins@finnobank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify: retention windows, backups, and explicit non-training guarantee

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful. Two quick clarifications so I can share with our legal team:

1) When you say snapshots are purged within 30 days after a deletion request, does that include cloud provider immutable snapshots (e.g., if vendor-managed backups have a separate retention)?
2) For the signed attestation: what fields are included? (time range covered, dataset identifiers, person signing).

If you can answer those two points and we get the DPA excerpt with the 7-day debug option, we’re very close to greenlighting a pilot.

- Anne
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Anne Collins <anne.collins@finnobank.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: retention windows, backups, and explicit non-training guarantee

Anne — quick answers below; we can provide the DPA excerpt and a draft attestation for signature within 48 hours.

1) Immutable cloud-provider snapshots:
   - If a backup was written to an immutable vendor snapshot store outside Redwood’s control, the effective deletion may be constrained by that provider’s retention. We track and surface those exceptions in the DPA and will commit to cooperating with you on off-cycle purges where the provider supports it. For most standard setups where Redwood controls snapshot lifecycle, we can commit to removing snapshots within 30 days post-deletion request.

2) Signed attestation contents (example fields):
   - Customer name and account id
   - Time range covered by the attestation
   - Types of data purged (request payloads, debug traces, snapshots)
   - Description of exclusion from training pipelines
   - The signatory name, title, and a timestamp

Next steps: I’ll send a DPA excerpt with the 7-day debug retention option and a draft attestation template (PDF) in a separate email. If you’d like that attestation signed by your legal contact rather than security, we can route appropriately.

If you want to lock the pilot schedule, Chloe — can you confirm the start date?

Thanks,
-Rishi
